deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous and next pages): Göttingen observatory, Tuesday 8 March 1836. These are observations of a freely swinging magnetometer needle to determine its logarithmic decrement (Decr. log.) with the induction circuit open ('offen') and closed ('geschlossen'/'geschl. Kette'). This page continues the series from oscillation 47 to 91; the next page continues it from 94 to 137.

Columns on each row: oscillation number n; clock time of a passage (10h m' s''); amplitude A_n in scale divisions (the arc read on the scale); and log10 A_n to 5 decimals.

The times show a constant period. Successive differences are about 42.25 to 42.45 s. Over the 12-oscillation gaps the averages are (23'38.3''-15'10.3'')/12 = 508.0/12 = 42.33 s and (40'34.55''-32'6.4'')/12 = 42.35 s. So T ≈ 42.33 s. Gauss does not compute T on this page.

Method (my explicit statement of what the numbers do):
(1) Group the logarithms in blocks of five consecutive oscillations n0-2 ... n0+2. Take the arithmetic mean M(n0), which stands for log A at the central oscillation n0.
(2) Pair two blocks whose centres are 16 oscillations apart. The logarithmic decrement per oscillation (Briggsian logarithms, in units of 1e-5) is λ = [M(n0) - M(n0+16)]/16.

Open circuit, n = 47-51 and 63-67:
- log A values: 2.94000, 2.93879, 2.93777, 2.93679, 2.93553. Mean = 14.68888/5 = 2.937776, written 2.93777.
- 2.92215, 2.92106, 2.92005, 2.91890, 2.91787. Mean = 14.60003/5 = 2.920006, written 2.92001.
- λ_open = (2.93777 - 2.92001)/16 = 0.01776/16 = 0.001110, i.e. 'D.L. = 111.0'.
- This agrees with the earlier open-circuit value 110.0 on the previous page and 116.50 on the next.

Circuit closed after n = 67 ('geschlossen'), n = 71-75 and 87-91:
- 2.89927, 2.89290, 2.88601, 2.87947, 2.87297. Mean = 14.43062/5 = 2.886124, written 2.88612.
- 2.79414, 2.78682, 2.78050, 2.77452, 2.76794. Mean = 13.90392/5 = 2.780784, written 2.78078.
- λ_closed = (2.88612 - 2.78078)/16 = 0.10534/16 = 0.0065838, i.e. 658.4. The transcription has 'Decr. log. 638.4'.
- The closed-circuit values on the neighbouring pages are 652.9 and 657.7.

Physical meaning (my gloss):
- Amplitudes decay geometrically, A_n = A_0·10^(-λn).
- With the circuit open, λ ≈ 0.00111 comes from air resistance and similar losses.
- Closing the circuit around the needle lets the induced currents damp the motion. That raises λ about six-fold, to ≈0.0066.
- The induction part of the damping is λ_closed - λ_open ≈ 0.00547 per oscillation.
- Alternating open and closed blocks (this page and the next) checks that the open-circuit damping stays stable, giving 110, 111, 116.5.

The right half of the image is the cut-off margin of the facing page. Its full content (n = 94-137) is the next page.
errors: Row 64: log10(833.85) = 2.92109, but Gauss wrote 2.92106. The value 2.92106 fits an amplitude of 833.80, so either the amplitude was misread/miswritten by 0.05 or the log is slightly off. The block mean 2.92001 is unaffected (2.920012 vs 2.920006).
Row 65: the amplitude was first written 829.65 (copying the next row) and corrected to 831.85. The logarithm 2.92005 belongs to the corrected value, so the correction is right.
Block means are truncated rather than rounded in places (2.937776 written 2.93777). This is negligible.

Decrement for the closed circuit: (2.88612 - 2.78078)/16 = 658.4 (in 1e-5), not 638.4. Either the transcription misreads the handwritten 5 as 3, or Gauss slipped. The neighbouring closed-circuit values 652.9 and 657.7 support 658.4.
All other logarithms check to within 1 unit in the 5th decimal.

results.what: Logarithmic decrement of a damped magnetometer oscillation, from means of five consecutive log-amplitudes at blocks 16 oscillations apart
results.modern_name: logarithmic decrement / exponential damping estimate (block-averaged least-squares-like estimator)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Intensitas vis magneticae, 1832; Resultate des magnetischen Vereins) and Weber

results.what: Comparison of damping with the induction circuit open vs closed: electromagnetic (eddy/induced-current) damping raises λ from ~0.00111 to ~0.0066 per oscillation
results.modern_name: electromagnetic induction damping (later Weber's 'Dämpfer'; damping as a measure of circuit resistance)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Wilhelm Weber, Göttingen 1830s; Weber's later absolute-resistance work (1850s)

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine laboratory data from the Gauss–Weber magnetism and induction program of 1836: logarithms of amplitudes, block means and decrement differences. The induction-damping experiments and the decrement method are well known as theirs. This is a raw observing sheet with no new theory.
transcription_corrections: The header 'ott.' above the time column is most likely 'off.' = offen (open circuit), matching 'offen' on the facing page.
The closed-circuit decrement 'Decr. log. 638.4' should probably read 658.4, which agrees with the computation (2.88612-2.78078)/16.
Row 89 time: '41 59.1' means 10h 41' 59.1'' (the minute is repeated in the MS); rows 90 and 91 are 42' and 43'.
Row numbers 63/64 are written over other digits (overwritten numbering), but the intended values are 63 and 64.
